newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland peace talks adjourned until September.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland peace talks adjourned until September.

text.p: Multi-party peace talks intended to end three decades of violence in Northern Ireland are being adjourned until September after the next round table session on Monday, the talks' chairman said on Wednesday.
The adjournment announced by former U.S. Senator George Mitchell came after Anglo-Irish proposals for disarming guerrilla groups were rejected by pro-British unionist political parties.
Mitchell said another round table session of the Belfast talks would be held on Monday but they would then adjourn until September.
"The plenary will resume next Monday at 4:00 pm (1500 GMT). Following that, the plenary will adjourn until September, with the first session then to occur not later that September 15," Mitchell said.
He said he would consult next week with all the participants and there would be an opportunity for bilateral discussions by them.
"We hope very much that this process will produce what the people of Northern Ireland want -- peace, political stability and reconciliation."
